news.title: Poland U-20 World Cup: Unlucky Falconets crash out of competition
news.lede: Nigeria’s Falconets have been eliminated from the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup after suffering a 1-0 defeat to Colombia in their quarter-final clash in Łódź, Poland, on Sunday. The decisive moment came deep into stoppage time when Valerin Loboa found the net in the 92nd minute to send Colombia into the semi-finals and end Nigeria’s campaign. The Falconets had been hoping to reach the last four for the first time since 2014 after securing an impressive 3-0 victory over England in the round of 16. Tosin Rafiu, Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei and Mary Mamudu scored for Nigeria in that encounter, while goalkeeper and captain Christiana Uzoma produced a standout display, including a penalty save.

news.title: Heartbreak in Lodz! Falconets Crash Out of U-20 World Cup After Late Colombia Strike
news.lede: Nigeria’s Falconets suffered heartbreaking elimination from the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup after Colombia scored a dramatic late winner to secure a narrow quarter-final victory. Sports247 reports that after an impressive run to the last eight, Nigeria were undone in the closing stages, with Valerin Loboa finding the decisive goal in the 90+2nd minute to send Colombia into the semi-finals. The defeat ended Nigeria’s hopes of reaching the last four of the competition for the first time since 2014. The Falconets had entered the quarter-final full of confidence after producing a commanding 3-0 victory over England in the Round of 16.

news.title: Cape Verde to Host CAF Strategy Conference, Bringing Together Africa’s 54 Member Associations' Presidents, Senior Men's, Women's & Youth National Team Coaches, and International Experts to Shape the Future of African Football
news.lede: The Confédération Africaine de Football (“CAF”) has announced that Cape Verde, whose inspiring FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign captured global attention, will host the CAF Strategy Conference from 7 to 9 October 2026 in Santa Maria, Sal Island. Convened under the leadership of CAF President Dr Patrice Motsepe, the Conference will bring together the Presidents of CAF’s 54 Member Associations, Zonal Union Presidents, CAF Executive Committee (EXCO) members, National Team coaches and international football experts. The landmark event will be structured around two pillars: strengthening football development and sustainability across Africa; and analysing the performances of Africa’s 10 FIFA World Cup 2026 representatives to prepare for even greater success at the FIFA World Cup 2030.

news.title: Does Football Unite the World?
news.lede: Widely considered one of the greatest shows on earth, the FIFA World Cup captivates the hearts of billions, promoting a sense of belonging, purpose, and, for many, an escape from daily life. This year, the crazed and colourful month of celebration culminated in a Argentina-Spain final enveloped by an ocean of 80,000 passionate voices wreathed in blue-white and red. This tournament has transcended all others to become an integrated cultural phenomenon. Even if you were just clocked in to the Haaland x Bellingham phenom, you made up the 70% of the world’s population this year’s FIFA World Cup was estimated to have captured.

news.title: Marcel Desailly: Why 1998 World Cup winner chose France over Ghana
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark YEN.com.gh as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Marcel Desailly, the Ghanaian-born French football legend, once sat down with Ghanaian sports journalist Kwabena Yeboah in 1995 to address one of the most talked-about decisions of his career: why he chose to wear the blue of France rather than the white or yellow of Ghana. Desailly was born in Accra in 1968 but relocated to France at the age of four. Growing up in the French system, he joined the Nantes academy as a teenager and progressed steadily through the country's youth football structures.
